disposition_reason: Two results tables print mean arsenic, chromium, lead and cadmium in beef from 20 Dhaka markets.

study.design: Two-phase market survey; one bulked sample (5 sub-samples) per market, 10 markets per phase
study.market: 20 markets of Dhaka City Corporation, Bangladesh

period.as_reported: November 2020 to December 2021 (samples stated as collected during 2021; phase 2 about two months after phase 1)

study.method: Dried, ground beef; microwave digestion with HNO3 and H2O2; flame and graphite-furnace AAS (Shimadzu AA-7000)
study.qa: Analytical blanks with each digestion batch; triplicate preparation; validated in-house methods; no CRM recoveries reported

controls.outcome: Pb 11.08-69.63 μg/kg across phase-1 markets and 22.64-46.74 μg/kg across phase-2 markets; Cd 4.07-19.32 μg/kg overall

unresolved: Text says phase-2 lead was lowest in BB (14.85 μg/kg), but the table gives BB lead 26.27 μg/kg and the lowest is AP 22.64 μg/kg; 14.85 is BB's cadmium value. Table values used.
The paper numbers both its limits table and its first results table as Table 1.
Market code MQM in the table, MQB in the footnote.
Dry versus fresh basis is not labelled in the results tables; basis taken as dry from the drying step.
No DOI is printed on the PDF.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Permissible limits cited for meat (Cd 0.5, Cr 0.05, Pb 0.10, As <0.50 mg/kg; FAO 1983, Codex 1994)

source_record_corrections: PDF prints no DOI; manifest DOI 10.37745/ejfst.2013/vol10n2pp110 corresponds to Vol.10, No.2, pp.1-10.
